title: Introduce heterogeneous cross-build proxy and stabilize toolchain versions
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: Our monolithic CI has grown slower and more brittle as we added more architectures (x86_64, arm64) and language runtimes. Teams frequently rebuild identical artifacts across runners and regions which inflates CI minutes and causes flakiness. The goal of this ticket is to introduce a lightweight cross-build proxy + artifact prebuild layer and simultaneously stabilize toolchain versions so builds are reproducible and cache-friendly.

Scope:
- Implement an HTTP/GRPC proxy service (prebuild-proxy) that acts as the canonical cache endpoint for prebuilt artifacts and cross-compiled wheels/binaries.
- Add a TTL and eviction policy for prebuilt artifacts with optional on-demand rebuild when a cache miss occurs.
- Standardize and pin toolchain images (gcc/clang, glibc, musl, Node.js, Python) for CI images and document upgrade cadence.
- Integrate BuildKit remote caching (S3-backed CAS) and make it the default for long-lived runners.
- Add a crossbuild matrix job to produce arm64 variants in a single pipeline using the proxy rather than triggering independent full pipelines.
- Replace a subset of base images with slim multi-stage + distroless variants and introduce reproducible build flags.

Why this differs from prior work: Previous efforts optimized cache configurations and consolidated builders but did not address cross-architecture duplication or the need for a canonical prebuild store with on-demand rebuild semantics. This ticket unifies those problems while adding guardrails for toolchain drift.
acceptance_criteria: Prebuild-proxy deployed to staging behind internal LB and reachable from CI runners
CI jobs successfully upload and fetch artifacts from proxy, reducing duplicate builds by >=30% in the arm64 matrix in the measured 2-week window
BuildKit remote cache enabled on non-ephemeral runners and validated by cache hit-rate dashboard (>=40% cache hit for long-lived flows)
Toolchain images (gcc/clang, Node 20.x, Python 3.11) are pinned in the internal toolchain repo and documented with an upgrade schedule
Demonstrable reproducible build for our core binary (same checksum across x86_64 and arm64 crossbuild using the proxy)
No regression in linting step; lint preflight added to each pipeline and passing on main branch
implementation_notes: Phase 1 (PoC): lightweight prebuild-proxy that stores artifacts in S3 with metadata index in PostgreSQL in staging. Expose a simple REST API: PUT /artifacts/:hash and GET with conditional rebuild header.
Phase 2: BuildKit integration for remote cache upload/download. Use ephemeral auth tokens from CI to write to proxy. Implement TTL-based eviction and metrics (size, hits, misses per artifact type).
Phase 3: Migrate arm64 build matrix to leverage crossbuild proxy; update pipeline templates to query proxy before executing heavy cross-compile steps.

Toolchain stabilization: create canonical toolchain images in registry.redwood.internal/toolchain/<lang>-<version>-<os>. Each image must include a toolchain-manifest file with deterministic versions and build flags.

Tradeoffs: Adding a proxy introduces operational surface (monitoring/HA). We mitigate with simple stateless frontends + S3 backing store and circuit-breaker to fallback to direct build if proxy unavailable.

Security: artifacts may contain build outputs. Use signed artifact manifests (HMAC) and enforce RBAC via CI service accounts. Requesting security review only if we enable cross-customer artifact sharing (not in this ticket).
Performance: Expect initial overhead of ~3-6s metadata checks per job, offset by large wins for cacheable layers and crossbuild reuse.

2026-01-22 - Luca Patel: PoC server up on staging cluster, basic PUT/GET implemented. Initial run showed 12% reduction in duplicate arm64 builds across two projects.
2026-02-03 - SRE (Ravi Singh): Observability hooks (Prometheus metrics and Grafana dashboard) merged. Need to add alert for artifact-store size growth.

2026-02-18 - CI Team (Aisha Romero): Updated pipeline templates to call proxy before heavy compile steps. Noticed intermittent 502s when proxy under load — added exponential backoff and fallback to local build.

2026-02-25 - QA (Noah Park): Reproducible build test added to nightly suite. Hit a checksum mismatch due to non-deterministic timestamp in packaging step; identified fix in packaging script (normalize mtimes).
2026-03-02 - Security (Lena Ortiz): Quick review done. Recommend HMAC-signed manifests and short-lived tokens for write access. No blocking issues; full review deferred.
2026-03-05 - Luca Patel: Enabled BuildKit remote cache on one pool. Early metrics show remote cache hit 38% for Python wheel builds. Roadmap updated to roll out to other pools after HA improvements.
